messages:
tara: quick check-in before tomorrow's roadmap sync I'm drafting the onramp checklist for tenant slicing (multi-region + isolation). want the minimum contract/pricing gates spelled out.
mike: +1. sales needs a short yes/no checklist for deal handoffs. keep it to 6 items max.
jess: engineering needs explicit acceptance criteria so we don't get half-signed promises. suggested gate list: automation, SLAs, telemetry, quality regression, pricing, commit terms.
raja: operations: also require a migration window + evacuation SLA. customers must pick a primary region and an allowed failover region.
tara: propose the handoff checklist (brief):
- infra automation: tenant deploy + evac scripts exist and ran once in staging
- SLA target: agreed p50/p95/p99 and fallback latency for failover region
- cost uplift estimate: console projection shown to customer and acknowledged
- model quality guardrails: fallback model variants defined + regression tests pass
- commit terms: reserved-capacity or 30-day opt-in for early pilots
- legal/compliance: residency & egress clause signed
mike: can we add a single-line explanation for each to the sales playbook? e.g., "cost uplift = expected % increase vs shared pool, inclusive of reservation premiums"
jess: technical knobs to present in product UI: preferred_region, allow_fallbacks (bool), max_cost_uplift_pct, fallback_sequence (list), reserved_commit_days. keep defaults conservative.
raja: telemetry events we need during pilot: routing_decision, fallback_reason, chosen_model_variant, token_cost_usd, eviction_event. these must be surfaced in the console with per-tenant breakdown.
billing-bot: FYI: when reserved_commit_days > 0, trigger billing plan schema entry and attach uplift line item. I'll post sample uplift bands after finance review.
tara: OK next steps: jess to add acceptance tests to infra repo (Wed), mike to draft one-page sales handoff language (Thu), raja to schedule a staging evacuation run (next Mon). We'll review in roadmap sync.
mike: thanks. short and actionable.
